chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim al-Khurasi (or al-Karkhi), from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah, from Atiyyah, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said:

The Prophet of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali, I have been granted nine characteristics due to you: three in this world, three in the Hereafter, two are for you, and one is what I fear for you. As for the three in this world, you are my Trustee, my Caliph over my people, and the judge of my religion. As for the three in the Hereafter, I will be given the Banner of Praise, and I will place it in your hand, and Adam and his progeny will be under my banner; you will assist me at the gates of Paradise, and I will grant you authority in my intercession for whomever you love. As for the two that are for you, you will not return as an unbeliever or go astray after me. And as for the one I fear for you, it is the treachery of Quraysh towards you after me, O Ali.'

key_terms.لَوَاءُ الْحَمْدِ: The Banner of Praise held by the Prophet in the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What are the nine characteristics granted to Ali (AS) by the Prophet according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* underscores the concept of *Fada'il* (virtues) by categorizing Ali’s (AS) status into worldly authority, eschatological honor, and personal fidelity. The 'feared' trait regarding Quraysh’s treachery highlights the historical tension between the Ahl al-Bayt and the early Caliphate, while the 'lawn al-Hamd' (Banner of Praise) signifies his unique role in the Hereafter. This narration serves as a foundational text for Shia claims of Ali’s exclusive spiritual and administrative succession.
